3. The plaintiffs petitioners filed a Misc. Case no. 02 of 2002 under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the Senior Assistant Judge, Nawabganj Sadar that the case of the plaintiffs petitioners in Misc. Case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in short inter alia that they were defendants nos. 25-30 in the original suit. The summons and notice of that suit were not served upon them. The plaintiffs of that suit is collusion with the process server of the court managed to show service of summons and notice upon them and managed to submit a false return to the court. Similarly they also managed to get the impugned judgment and decree by practicing fraud upon the court. The petitioners were not at all aware of the original suit. As such they could not appear and contest the suit, that they came to know about that judgment and decree for the first time as 08.01.2002 A.D. The petitioners have been seriously prejudiced by the impugned judgment and decree. Hence, they have filed the Misc. Case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 4. The defendants opposite party nos. 1-3 contested the Misc. Case by filing a joint written objection alleging that the case is not the case is not maintainable in the present form. The cause of action of the same has not arisen. It is barred by limitation and hence, the case is liable to be disallowed with costs. According to the contesting opposite party, the material facts of the case are that the summonses and notices of the original suit were duly served upon the petitioners of this case. In spite of that they refrained from contesting that the suit and then the court has passed the impugned judgment and decree. Thereafter the court on application of the opposite party appointed an Advocate Commissioner for making their sharers portioned by metes and bound. On 04.08.2000 A.D. The petitioners were aware of all of these facts. In spite of that they have brought the instant case only with an ill motive to harass the opposite parties. Hence they prayed for rejection of Misc. Case. 

 5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chapai Nawabganj who tried the Misc. Case under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure rejected the same by his order dated 19.04.2003 in Misc. Case no. 2 of 2002. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 19.04.2003 in Misc. Case no. 2 of 2002 the plaintiffs petitioners preferred an appeal before the District Judge, at Nawabganj which was heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court Chapai Nawabganj and he was pleased to dismiss the appeal by his judgment. 

 6. The plaintiff’s petitioners examined 2 P.Ws while the defendants opposite parties did not adduce any evidence in Miscellaneous Case final under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with-the judgment and order dated 04.04.2004 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court of Nawabganj in Miscellaneous Appeal no. 23 of 2003 the petitioners preferred the instant revisional application under section 115(1) application before this Hon'ble Court and obtained the present rule. 

 9. Mr. Md. Shahadat Tanveer Amin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the summons of the case was not served upon the defendants petitioners. The learned Joint District Judge, committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure wrongly held that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation. 

 10. He next submits that the court below erred in law in not accepting the date of knowledge of the ex-parte disposal of the suit and holding that the Miscellaneous Case has been filed out of the statutory period of limitation. 

 11. He further submits that the court below misread the evidence of the plaintiff’s petitioners and as such arrived at an erroneous decision. The court of appeal below did not apply its mind in the facts and circumstances of the case and as such totally misdirected in passing the judgment. The judgment and order of the court of appeal below has been based on mere conjecture and surmises and not based on materials on record. He submits that the judgment and order passed by the court of appeal below arc neither proper nor in accordance with law. 

 13. Learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of his contention has referred the case of Soni Gopal Das and others Vs. Mohd. Habibullah, reported in 9 MLR (AD) page 158. He next referred the case of Asuk Kumar Mistry and others Vs. Shwrabi Bewa and others reported in 10 MLR (HC) page 177. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further referred the case of Sabura Khatun and others Vs. Wahab and others reported in II MLR (AD) page 411. The learned Advocate for the petitioner lastly referred the case of Ryder Ali Mia Vs. Razia Begum and others reported in 12 BLC (AD) page 75. 

 14. I have heard the learned Advocate and perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court Chapainawabgonj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 2003 affirming the judgment and order dated 19.04.2003 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Nawabgonj Sadar in Miscellaneous Case no. 2 of 2002 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure arising out of Other Class Suit no. 64 of 1996 in a suit for partition the Miscellaneous Case was contested by the opposite party nos. 1-3 by filing a joint written objection and the learned Trial Judge rejected the Miscellaneous Case filed Under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure vide order dated 19.04.2003. Being aggrieved the petitioners preferred an appeal before the District Judge at Nawabganj which was heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court Chapai Nawabgonj and he was pleased to dismiss the appeal in affirming the judgment and order dated 04.04.2004 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal no. 23 of 2003. 

 15. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order of the last court of fact I find the same has suffered from serious miscarriage of justice which has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case filed Under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and wrongly held that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation. 

 16. I also find that the learned court below erred in law in not accepting the date of knowledge of the ex-parte disposal of the suit and holding that the Miscellaneous Case has been barred by limitation. 

 17. In order to arrive at a proper finding it is very much pertinent to refer the case of Hyder Ali Mia Vs. Razia Begum and others reported in 12 BLC (AD) page 75 where our Apex Court held that:- 

 "None of the OPWs stated a single word on the service of summons on defendant no. 1 but the records show that after the receipt of the return the trial court fixed a date for ex-parte disposal but before fixing the date, the trial court has not looked into the service return. "The records of the trial court do not show that the provisions of rule 19B of Order V of the Code has been complied with and even in the records there is no materials showing sending of the summons by registered post with acknowledgment due and there is also nothing on record to indicate that the postal acknowledgment due was received by the trial court and no step was also taken by the respondent to examine the postal peon to prove the service of summons which was sent by registered post with A/D. in the present case in a hot haste an ex-parte decree was obtained which indicates that a fraud was committed upon the court as well as upon the defendants and when a fraud is proved, then there is no question of limitation and time will run from the date when the fraud is detected and so, the question of limitation and time will run from the date when the fraud is detected and so the question of limitation does not arise in the present case; even as, for argument's sake, it is conceded that the fraud was detected earlier, even then the court is not debarred to interfere under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure." 

 18. In the case of Sabura Khatun and others Vs. Abdul Wahab and others reported in 11 MLR (AD) 411 where our Apex Court held that:- 

 20. In the case of Asuk Kumar Mistry and other Vs. Shwrabi Bewa and others reported in 10 MLR12 (HC) page 117 it is held that:- 

 "I perused the documents on record and the cited decisions which lends support to the submissions made by the learned lawyer for the opposite party. I found that the defendants opposite party was prevented by Sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the suit was taken up for ex-parte hearing. The learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd court Khulna committed no error of law in allowing the Miscellaneous Case under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such calls for no interference by this court. 

 21. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 20.010.1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court Khulna, in Misc. Case no. 11 of 1995 is hereby affirmed. 

 22. In the case of Soni Gopal Dash and another Vs. Mohd. Habibullah, reported in 9 MLR page 158 where our Apex Court held that:-Our considered view is that .when the signature of Shahid son of the defendant upon whom summons of the suit admittedly is said to have been served, since has been challenged by the defendant definitely the onus was upon the plaintiffs to prove the same beyond doubt and the trial court was also under the legal obligation to ensure about the same comparing the admitted signature of Shahid with his disputed signatures in Ext. Ka(1) and Ext. ka(2). 

 24. On due and proper consideration of the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of revisional application and the citations as referred by the learned Advocate in course of his submissions. I find substance and merit in the rule. The citations as referred by the learned Advocate in support of his contention are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 25. Accordingly, the rule is made absolute, there will be no order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 04.01.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge. 1st court Chapainawabgonj in Miscellaneous Appeal no. 23 of 2003 affirming the judgment and order dated 19.04.2003 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chapainawabgonj Sadar in Miscellaneous Case no. 2 of 2002 are hereby set aside and consequently the Other Class suit no. 64 of 1996 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge Chapainawabgonj is hereby restored to its original file number and the learned trial court is hereby directed to dispose of the Other Class suit no. 64 of 1996 expeditiously within 3 months from the date of receipt of the order.
